title: The price you paid
hook: Should your old purchase price change today's listing?

knows: basic arithmetic and reading a small table
doesNotKnow: Distinguish a seller's historical reference point from the current market offer.

misconception: The quantities in this case can be combined without checking their reference, denominator, or information boundary.
objective: Distinguish a seller's historical reference point from the current market offer.
keyState: Both complete computed cases are visible as retained observations; the question-case picture survives Reset.

claims.text: You paid €180k and receive a €160k offer. Relative to your purchase price, what is the gain or loss? Toy inputs A=[180, 160]; B=[140, 160].
claims.source: Local explicit hypothetical assumptions in spec.ts and model.ts; not participant measurements.

claims.text: Computed results: [[-20, 160, 180], [20, 160, 140]]. Labels: Gain €k, Offer €k, Paid €k.
claims.source: compute() in the lesson-local model.ts; finite numeric operations over the explicit inputs.

claims.text: Changing the historical purchase price changes the seller’s reference-point gain. It does not change the current offer. These two quantities should remain separate when interpreting an asking price.
claims.source: The two controlled cases in spec.ts; scope limited to these toy inputs and displayed model rule.

claims.text: A new toy case uses Paid €k=140, Offer €k=160. What is Gain €k? Answer: 20.
claims.source: compute() applied to the contrasting new input case; source list is an idea pointer only.

recall.question: A new toy case uses Paid €k=140, Offer €k=160. What is Gain €k?
recall.why: Applying the stated toy rule to the new inputs gives 20. The result depends on these assumptions; it is not a universal behavioral response.

sourceProvenance.text: Boston condo owners facing a nominal loss set higher asking prices and waited longer to sell (Genesove & Mayer, 2001).
sourceProvenance.caveat: Original list says figures are approximate and papers were not individually rechecked. No empirical source is verified by this build.

meaningfulDifference: Distinguish a seller's historical reference point from the current market offer.
